text: ks_comparison list named slots; can read directly scripting QC dashboards: cmp$schema_diff – one row per column pair (matched, base-, comp-) kind_match, label_match, format_match. cmp$row_diff – one row per matched / unmatched row key_id, base_row, comp_row, status. cmp$value_diff – one row per differing cell kind, base, comp, diff, note. as_tibble(cmp) ks_tidy(cmp). cmp$pattern_summary – recurring shapes per column (e.g. case_only, constant_offset) find_patterns = TRUE requested; otherwise empty tibble usual columns. cmp$unmatched_rows – full base-/ comp-observations, capped max_unmatched_rows. cmp$first_last_unequal – PROC COMPARE-style first / last differing observations per matched column. cmp$meta – counts, key columns, row-matching strategy, rendered key labels used reports. cmp$manifest – input hashes + run timestamp QC traceability. cmp$verdict – executive headline used print(cmp) HTML report.

title: Getting started with ksCompare
text: Per-column overrides: ULP tolerance useful want absorb floating-point round-trip noise:
code: ks_compare(   data.frame(id = 1, x = 1.0),   data.frame(id = 1, x = 1.0001),   by = "id",   tolerance = ks_tol(abs = 1e-3) ) #> ✔ data.frame(id = 1, x = 1) vs data.frame(id = 1, x = #> 1.0001) — identical ks_tol(   abs = 0,   per_column = list(     weight = ks_tol(abs = 0.01),     height = ks_tol(rel = 0.001)   ) ) ks_compare(base, comp, by = "id", tolerance = ks_tol(ulp = 4))

title: Getting started with ksCompare
text: ks_comp_options() controls semantics apply columns: na_equal: treat NA == NA equal (default TRUE). sas_special_missing: distinguish .-.Z ._ SAS missings (haven-imported numerics ). compare_labels / compare_formats: schema-level checks. Format comparison trailing-dot- case-tolerant (DATE9. == DATE9 == date9.). str_trim, str_case, str_norm: string normalisation. Strings always compared encoding-safely (Latin1 vs UTF-8 produce false diffs). tz: "preserve" (default), "UTC", "strip" POSIXct.
code: ks_compare(   base, comp, by = "id",   options = ks_comp_options(str_trim = TRUE, str_case = "fold") )

code: # Sample data with intentional errors adsl <- tibble(   USUBJID = sprintf("01-%03d", 1:6),   AGE = c(34, 52, -1, -3, 29, 70),   SEX = c("M", "F", "M", NA, "F", "X"),   WEIGHT = c(70, 80, 75, 500, 65, 68) )

title: Powerful Data Validation Engine
text: Best practice: Group related rules together use descriptive names. mandatory, named rules improve code maintainability make debugging easier: Let’s extend rules advanced expressions. can use regular expressions easily: Apply rules first-failing mode: Apply rules collecting failures:
code: # Define validation rules rules <- list(   # Rule 1: Age must be non-negative   age_non_negative = list(     expr = ~ AGE < 0,     msg = "AGE must be non-negative"   ),      # Rule 2: SEX cannot be missing   sex_not_missing = list(     expr = ~ is.na(SEX),     msg = "SEX is missing"   ),      # Rule 3: SEX must be M or F (ignoring missing)   sex_valid = list(     expr = ~ !is.na(SEX) & !(SEX %in% c("M", "F")),     msg = "SEX must be M/F"   ),      # Rule 4: WEIGHT within reasonable range   weight_range = list(     expr = ~ WEIGHT > 300,     msg = "WEIGHT out of range"   ) ) rules <- append(rules, list(   # --- Study Subject Identifier ---   usubjid_format = list(     expr = ~ !grepl("^\\d{2}-\\d{3}$", USUBJID),     msg = "USUBJID must match format: XX-XXX-XXX"   ) ))  ks_check_rules(adsl, rules, mode = "all") |>    ks_collapse_check_msgs(col = check_msgs) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   USUBJID   AGE SEX   WEIGHT check_msgs                                          #>   <chr>   <dbl> <chr>  <dbl> <chr>                                               #> 1 01-001     34 M         70 OK                                                  #> 2 01-002     52 F         80 OK                                                  #> 3 01-003     -1 M         75 AGE must be non-negative                            #> 4 01-004     -3 NA       500 AGE must be non-negative; SEX is missing; WEIGHT o… #> 5 01-005     29 F         65 OK                                                  #> 6 01-006     70 X         68 SEX must be M/F result_first <- ks_check_rules(adsl, rules, mode = "first") |>    ks_collapse_check_msgs(col = check_msgs)  result_first[, c("USUBJID", "check_msgs")] #> # A tibble: 6 × 2 #>   USUBJID check_msgs               #>   <chr>   <chr>                    #> 1 01-001  OK                       #> 2 01-002  OK                       #> 3 01-003  AGE must be non-negative #> 4 01-004  AGE must be non-negative #> 5 01-005  OK                       #> 6 01-006  SEX must be M/F result_all <- ks_check_rules(adsl, rules, mode = "all") |>    ks_collapse_check_msgs(col = check_msgs)  result_all[, c("USUBJID", "check_msgs")] #> # A tibble: 6 × 2 #>   USUBJID check_msgs                                                    #>   <chr>   <chr>                                                         #> 1 01-001  OK                                                            #> 2 01-002  OK                                                            #> 3 01-003  AGE must be non-negative                                      #> 4 01-004  AGE must be non-negative; SEX is missing; WEIGHT out of range #> 5 01-005  OK                                                            #> 6 01-006  SEX must be M/F

code: # Using rlang expressions for dynamic rules dynamic_age <- function(threshold_age) {   list(     age_threshold = list(       expr = rlang::new_formula(         lhs = NULL,         rhs = rlang::expr(AGE < !!threshold_age)       ),       msg = sprintf(         "Age must be at least %d years",         threshold_age       )     )   ) }  # Define rule validation_age <- dynamic_age(18) rlang::eval_tidy(   rlang::f_rhs(validation_age$age_threshold$expr),   data = adsl ) #> [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE # Expected: # [1] FALSE FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE FALSE  result <- ks_check_rules(adsl, validation_age) result |> mutate(     check_msgs = purrr::map_chr(check_msgs, ~ paste(.x, collapse = ", "))   ) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   USUBJID   AGE SEX   WEIGHT check_msgs                    #>   <chr>   <dbl> <chr>  <dbl> <chr>                         #> 1 01-001     34 M         70 OK                            #> 2 01-002     52 F         80 OK                            #> 3 01-003     -1 M         75 Age must be at least 18 years #> 4 01-004     -3 NA       500 Age must be at least 18 years #> 5 01-005     29 F         65 OK                            #> 6 01-006     70 X         68 OK

code: # For a single-row heatmap-like display, add a constant y value. visualize_results1 <- function(df) {    df <- df %>%     mutate(       status = factor(         ifelse(           purrr::map_lgl(check_msgs, ~ "OK" %in% .x),           "Valid",           "Invalid"         ),         levels = c("Valid", "Invalid")       ),       y = "Subjects"     )    ggplot(df, aes(x = USUBJID, y = y, fill = status)) +     geom_tile(height = 0.6, color = "white") +     scale_fill_manual(       values = c(         Valid = "#2ecc71",         Invalid = "#e74c3c"       )     ) +     labs(x = "Subject", y = NULL, fill = "Status") +     theme_minimal() +     theme(       axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)     ) }  # Alternative: Bar chart (usually more informative) visualize_results2 <- function(df) {    df %>%     mutate(       status = ifelse(         purrr::map_lgl(check_msgs, ~ "OK" %in% .x),         "Valid",         "Invalid"       )     ) %>%     ggplot(aes(status, fill = status)) +     geom_bar() +     scale_fill_manual(       values = c(         Valid = "#2ecc71",         Invalid = "#e74c3c"       )     ) +     labs(       x = NULL,       y = "Number of records",       fill = "Status"     ) +     theme_minimal() }  # Alternative: Show number of violations per subject # If subjects can have multiple violations, this is often the most useful diagnostic plot:  visualize_results3 <- function(df) {    df %>%     mutate(       n_violations = purrr::map_int(         check_msgs,         ~ if ("OK" %in% .x) 0L else length(.x)       )     ) %>%     ggplot(aes(reorder(USUBJID, n_violations), n_violations)) +     geom_col() +     coord_flip() +     labs(       x = "Subject",       y = "Number of violations"     ) +     theme_minimal() }  # Example visualization visualize_results1(validation_result) visualize_results2(validation_result) visualize_results3(validation_result)

Optional column name(s) use matching key. NULL (default): rows matched row position. warning banner shown HTML report never silent. character: column name sides. Use named vector key renamed: c(USUBJID = "SUBJID"). "auto": search smallest combination shared columns unique sides (capped 4 columns). Falls back position match warning nothing qualifies. mapping Optional explicit column mapping renamed columns. Either fully named character vector (c(base_col = "comp_col", ...)) 2-column data frame columns base comp. Mapping pairs always win exact-name matching. tolerance ks_tol() specification. Defaults strict equality. Per-column overrides supported via ks_tol(per_column = list(col = ks_tol(...))). coerce Type-coercion strictness. One : "safe" (default): vctrs::vec_ptype2() plus integer↔double, factor↔character, haven_labelled unwrapping. "strict": common types vctrs::vec_ptype2() agrees . Type mismatches surface kind = "type_mismatch" rows. "lossy": additionally allows numeric↔character, date/datetime↔character (ISO-8601), factor↔integer (level codes). dup_keys Strategy duplicate keys (per-side independently). One : "first" (default): keep first occurrence per side. Drops rows; emits ksCompare_dup_keys_resolved info message. "last": keep last occurrence per side. message. "keep_all": pair duplicate rows positionally within key group (1↔1, 2↔2, …). Leftover rows longer side become base- compare-. FALSE, cmp$pattern_summary empty tibble usual column layout. n_first_last Non-negative integer (default 5). Per matched column least one cell diff, capture first last n_first_last differences key_id order cmp$first_last_unequal. Mirrors First / Last N Obs Compared Variables Unequal tables SAS PROC COMPARE. title: Compare two data frames — ks_compare
text: ks_comparison object components: meta: counts, keys, matching strategy, row-key lookup table. schema_diff: one row per matched / unmatched column kind / label / format comparison. key_diff: counts matched / base-/ comp-rows. row_diff: long table key_id, base_row, comp_row, status. value_diff: long table differing cells column_base, column_comp, kind, base, comp, diff, note. pattern_summary: detected recurring shapes per column (populated find_patterns = TRUE; otherwise empty tibble standard column layout). unmatched_rows: full base-/ comp-rows (capped max_unmatched_rows); see ks_unmatched_rows(). first_last_unequal: per-column first / last n_first_last differing observations key_id order (PROC COMPARE-style). verdict: list headline (character), severity ("ok", "info", "warn", "critical"), pct_match (0–100 numeric), n_cells, n_diffs; summary shown print(). options, tolerance: inputs (echoed manifest). manifest: input hashes + run metadata. Inspect print(), summary(), tibble::as_tibble(), render via ks_report_html() / ks_report_xlsx().

title: Compare two data frames — ks_compare
text: Schema alignment — columns paired explicit mapping first, exact name match. Unmatched columns become base_only / comp_only reported cmp$schema_diff. Key resolution — taken literally supplied, auto-inferred shared columns = "auto", rows matched row position = NULL. Row matching — keyed-unique join, duplicate-key resolution (dup_keys), position-zip; details land cmp$meta$matching (also displayed print() HTML report). Cell diff — per-column equality respecting ks_tol() (abs / rel / ULP) numerics, ks_comp_options() strings / NAs / SAS special missings, vctrs::vec_cast() compatible types. Pattern detection — recurring shapes across diffs (constant offset, sign flip, trim-, …) scored surfaced cmp$pattern_summary. Manifest — xxhash64 digests inputs / options / tolerance plus timestamp package version, QC traceability.
